metadata.title: Why Two Identical Anti-HER2 Drugs Kill Completely Different Tumors
metadata.purpose: vox-explainer slate cut of Cancer Nanomedicine candidate 01. Source: cancer-nanomedicine/chapters/05-antibody-drug-conjugates-as-nanoscale-medicines.md
metadata.color_semantics: TEAL = membrane-permeable payload / bystander spread / T-DXd; CRIMSON = killed cells / confined payload / T-DM1 failure in HER2-low; GOLD = key mechanism highlight
metadata.note: EXCLUSIONS: Cut DAR, the five-step dose-loss funnel, linker chemistry details, pneumonitis toxicity, and the DAR-8 failure. Show ONLY: same antibody, one payload stays put, one spreads.

beats.narration_text: A breast cancer patient's tumor tests HER2-low. One drug is approved for it. The other is not. Both carry the exact same HER2-targeting antibody.

card.sub: One drug approved for HER2-low. One not. Both carry the same antibody.

beats.narration_text: T-DM1 and T-DXd. Identical antibodies. One opens a new disease category. One does not. The targeting mechanism is not the differentiator.

props.title: T-DM1 vs T-DXd — identical antibodies, split outcomes

items.label: T-DM1
items.sub: Anti-HER2 antibody + linker + payload — does not treat HER2-low

items.label: T-DXd
items.sub: Same anti-HER2 antibody — opens a new disease category (HER2-low)

items.label: Where the difference is not
items.sub: Antibodies identical — the split cannot be in the targeting

production_viz.label: two drugs, identical antibodies

beats.narration_text: Two drugs. Same antibody. One treats HER2-low tumors. The other cannot. The antibody is identical. What determines the outcome?

beats.narration_text: The antibody controls one step only: which cell gets bound. In a HER2-low tumor, few cells carry the antigen. Most do not. The antibody cannot reach them.

props.title: The antibody controls exactly one step

items.label: What the antibody does
items.sub: Chooses which cell gets bound — one job, one step

items.label: HER2-positive cells
items.sub: In a HER2-low tumor, only a few cells carry the antigen

items.label: The majority
items.sub: Most cells in the tumor are HER2-negative — the antibody never binds them

production_viz.label: the antibody controls one step
production_viz.mechanic: a HER2-low tumor patch shown as a grid of ~30 cells; a few teal cells are HER2-positive; a single Y-shaped antibody attaches to one teal cell. The gray HER2-negative cells outnumber the teal cells ~5:1.
production_viz.note: show the antigen scarcity visually; do not spread payload yet

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] HER2-low patch: antibody binds the few teal cells only

beats.narration_text: Default assumption: both drugs underperform equally in HER2-low tumors. Antigen is scarce, little binds, little kills. Choose whichever the patient tolerates better. That assumption is wrong.

document.quote: Default assumption: both drugs underperform equally in HER2-low tumors. That assumption is wrong.

beats.new_visual_element: [DOCUMENT] quote: the default assumption is wrong

beats.narration_text: T-DM1 uses a non-cleavable linker. After the antibody binds and the conjugate enters the cell, the freed payload carries a charged fragment. Charged molecules cannot cross the cell membrane.

props.title: T-DM1 — non-cleavable linker traps the payload

items.label: The linker
items.sub: Non-cleavable — releases only after the drug is inside a cell

items.label: The freed payload
items.sub: Carries a charged fragment left over from the linker

items.label: What charge means
items.sub: Charged molecules cannot cross the lipid cell membrane

production_viz.label: T-DM1: non-cleavable linker, payload trapped
production_viz.mechanic: single cell in cross-section; the T-DM1 conjugate enters via endocytosis; inside, the linker releases the payload; the payload carries a small crimson '+' charge tag; arrows toward the membrane bounce back — the payload cannot escape.
production_viz.note: the '+' tag is the mechanism: charge = confinement

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] T-DM1 in a cell — charged payload bounces off the membrane

beats.narration_text: T-DM1 therefore kills only the cell it entered. HER2-negative neighbors — the majority in a HER2-low tumor — survive untouched.

lines: T-DM1 kills only the cell it entered.
HER2-negative neighbors — the majority in HER2-low — survive.
One binding equals one kill. No spread.

beats.new_visual_element: [FORMACARD] one binding, one kill, no spread

beats.narration_text: T-DXd uses a cleavable linker and its freed payload is membrane-permeable. Released inside a HER2-positive cell, it diffuses across the membrane into neighboring cells.

props.title: T-DXd — cleavable linker frees a permeable payload

items.label: The linker
items.sub: Cleavable — releases the payload cleanly, no charged leftover

items.label: The freed payload
items.sub: Membrane-permeable — neutral, crosses the lipid bilayer freely

items.label: The bystander effect
items.sub: Diffuses out of the bound cell into surrounding neighbors

production_viz.label: T-DXd: cleavable linker, payload permeable
production_viz.mechanic: single teal cell in cross-section; payload released inside; teal payload molecules diffuse outward through the membrane into three neighboring gray cells; each neighbor turns crimson as the payload accumulates.
production_viz.note: the bystander effect visible as neighboring cells changing color

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] T-DXd payload diffuses across the membrane — bystander effect

beats.narration_text: The antibody is not the complete mechanism. It locates the cell. What happens next depends entirely on whether the payload can cross a membrane — and that is a linker and payload property, not an antibody property.

document.quote: The antibody is not the complete mechanism. It locates the cell. What happens next is a linker and payload property, not an antibody property.

beats.new_visual_element: [DOCUMENT] quote: kill radius is a linker property, not an antibody property

beats.narration_text: HER2-low tumor patch: five HER2-positive cells available to the antibody. T-DM1 kills those five. T-DXd from the same five entry points spreads membrane-permeable payload to roughly forty surrounding cells. Same antibody. Eight times more kills.

props.title: HER2-low patch — same 5 entry points, different kill count

items.label: Antibody reach
items.sub: Same 5 HER2-positive cells — all the antibody can bind in the patch

items.label: T-DM1
items.sub: Kills the 5 bound cells — payload stays put

items.label: T-DXd
items.sub: Spreads into ~40 surrounding cells — 8x more kills

production_viz.label: HER2-low patch: 5 entry points, 5 vs ~40 kills
production_viz.mechanic: same HER2-low grid from B04. Five teal HER2-positive cells receive the antibody. Left panel (T-DM1): five crimson X-marks on the five entry cells only. Right panel (T-DXd): five entry cells go crimson, then a diffusion ring spreads outward, turning ~40 surrounding cells crimson. Big label at bottom: 5 vs ~40 (8x).
production_viz.note: the whole reel converges on this one image

beats.new_visual_element: [GRAPHIC] HER2-low patch — 5 T-DM1 kills vs ~40 T-DXd kills

beats.narration_text: Same antibody. T-DM1 payload stays confined by charge. T-DXd payload spreads via membrane permeability. That linker-and-payload difference — not the antibody — is why T-DXd treats HER2-low breast cancer and T-DM1 does not.

lines: T-DXd payload — spreads by membrane permeability.
